_doc: Milford Road Course (unofficial) through Lake Murray v4's engine (ledger 0078). The line, widths and profile are tracks/milford-road-course's (installed 0.6.0), read by tools/lm_engine_intake.py; the profile is the measured one with the elevation stage's grade cap undone; the camber is the G10 lidar survey (source/lidar/camber-survey/crossfall.json); the edge is the circuit's (no curb, no sidewalk). Every other key is the live track's, copied; the live config is untouched.

bespoke._pads_shade_doc: ledger 0100 item 6 (Kevin 2026-11-22, the track file: "Shrink it"): tools/seat_pads_blend.py shades the 20 rebuilt pads smooth, each vertex's normal the area-weighted mean of its faces' (tools/pad_clip.area_normals), so the kn5 writer keeps one vertex per pad vertex instead of three per triangle (0.1.13: 247,197 writer vertices for 82,408 triangles, +11.37 MB). Measured on the Mac on the 0.1.5 prepped ground's ride pad (5,837 triangles): writer vertices 17,511 -> 3,041 (-82.6 %); positions and UVs identical; the shading normal moves p50 0.015 / p95 0.28 / p99 0.95 deg by area, at most 3.25 deg on any face over 10 cm2, 0.095 % of the area over 2 deg (the 1GRASS ground under it is smooth-shaded already); no UV seam (world-planar UVs). Expected on 0.1.14 [modelled from the PC's apron_9, 1,991 vertices for 3,567 triangles, and that ride pad]: about 43,000-46,000 writer vertices, -8.9 to -9.0 MB
bespoke._pads_seat_doc: ledger 0092 (the 2026-11-18 scenery audit, item 3: ~16,900 m2 of pavement within 30 m drawn as turf): the ride pad and the 19 paved blobs beside the lap (source/runoff/scripts/runoff_pads.py: class D or NAIP grey, outlined in the road's frame from the edge strip's lip, source/runoff/runoff_pads.json) rebuilt on the PREPPED ground's own triangles 6 cm over it (tools/seat_pads_blend.py, Nevada's route, ledger 0081) and named 1RUNOFF_apron_<k>: paved run-off physics (surfaces.ini RUNOFF), the concrete skin (texture_overrides 1RUNOFF)

grassfx_zones._max_rects_doc: Milford 0.1.5 (ledger 0082 Owed 4): every rectangle the reading makes (1,285 at 12 m cells), no cap. 0.1.3's 96 [invented, 0.1.0's 48 doubled] covered 64 % of the measured wood floor C, 16 % of long grass B and 16 % of no grass D; all of them cover 92 / 67 / 71 % (source/vegetation/scripts/grass_coverage.py). source._note: Traced 2026-10-28 off USDA NAIP 2022-08-16 (0.6 m native; tile m_4208327_ne_17_060_20220816), exported from the USGS NAIPImagery ImageServer as an EPSG:4326 north-up clip, bbox -83.6700,42.5630,-83.6570,42.5770 at 2130x3112 (0.5 m/px) = source/naip_2022_mrc.jpg. Paved surface classified by colour, centre line found by a centre-seeking shortest path between hand-placed waypoints (source/trace/F1.json), re-centred and width-measured by perpendicular scans every 2 m. Widths clamped 9-16 m (median 11; the west front straight 16). Tree-shadowed pavement on the east side added by colour (source/trace/shadow_patch.py). Re-run: source/trace/README.md. CORRECTED 2026-10-31 (source/trace/unsquash_frame.py): the export has square-degree pixels, its true extent is lat 42.56050..42.57950, and the trace had read it squashed north-south by 0.737; OSM's outline, which this note used to call mis-drawn, was right. Length now 4.91 km vs GM's '2.9 mi' (4.67 km), +5 %; see source/route-notes.md. CORRECTED 2026-11-03 (source/trace/apron_corner.py, ledger 0069): at the left-hander about s 1,000 the scans had read the concrete run-off apron outside the corner as road (up to 21.4 m wide, the line on the asphalt's outer edge); fixes 383-424 keep their inner edge and take the road's own 11.28 m, the centre moving up to 4.7 m inside. Lap 4.90 km.

road_profile._doc: No banking authored (L10). Deck follows bare-earth 3DEP; any real cross-slope comes from lidar sections, never from curvature. The lap IS banked: 1 m lidar sections read -4.3 % in the esses (s 620), -7.1 % at the U-turn (s 780, the likeliest Carousel), +8.0 % at s 995. Tried 2026-10-28: scripts.elevation.crossfall (measured, 6 % cap, 80 % of the lap banked) made drive_test WORSE than the flat deck (ground-on-top 14 -> 53, severe steps 7 -> 17, bumps 17.2 -> 89.7/km, excursion drops 31 -> 52), the ledger-0018 class (crossfall x width steps). data/crossfall.json removed; the banks are authoring work, not a flag.
road_profile._ribbon_cols_doc: 2026-11-03, ledger 0069: 4 lateral columns, so a row's quad cannot twist on a tight corner that descends. The left-hander at s 1,000 drops 13-15 % round a 13 m radius; with one quad per row the inside edge's rows bunch towards the turning centre while each row drops the full 0.4 m, and the quad's diagonal laid that drop across the centre wheel paths as a step every 3 m (drive_test: the lap's severe steps and most of its kinks). Unbanked: build_mesh honours the key on a flat road since 0069. Not a gate change.
road_profile._max_grade_doc: Set so it never binds (L3; Kevin: real hills are never reshaped). At the 9 % default the cap shaved the real hill: the deck sat up to 5.96 m under the lidar at the SW corner and 1.6 m in the esses, and drive_test failed on grass over the pavement lip and drops off the edge (2026-10-28). The despiked 3DEP profile climbs 26.6 % over 21 m at s 3,650 (31 % over one 3 m step): the climb from the bottom sweeper to the front straight, cut into a hillside (lidar cross-sections: ground 2-3 m lower 20 m left, 1-2 m higher 20 m right, both edges climbing with the line). The 2 m dip at s 3,605 is the service-road underpass, removed by the 33 m despike.
road_profile._ribbon_cols_dropped: the live track's build_mesh ribbon columns (ledger 0069); the v021 assembler never reads the key (its twist answer is tools/densify_ribbon_blend.py), so the port does not carry it (ledger 0078)

route._orientation_doc: Clockwise, per the OSM oneway tags on every raceway way here (unverified against onboard video). S/F on the 16 m west front straight about 2/3 of the way up, raced north; the grid sits on the ~250 m of straight behind it. The lap: west straight N -> NW corner -> right-hand hairpin off the apron -> esses south -> U-turn -> north -> east into the serpentine round the woods -> top straight E -> NE corner -> east side S -> sweeping bottom W -> SW corner. Unused pavement (later layouts over this kn5): the inner hairpin short-cut, the top-straight bypass, the SE back section + cross-connector + hook.
route._smooth_sigma_y_doc: 0.1.12: 0, the line's heights are lm_intake.measured_surface's filtered surface (it refuses any other value); was 3.0 (4.5 m) over the 3DEP profile

edge._doc: the circuit edge (ledger 0078): no curb, no sidewalk. edge._grass_clearance_doc: 0.1.6 (PC, 2026-11-08; Kevin: "Milford still looks messy on the edges of the high speed curves"): the strip's outer lip 2 cm under the lane edge (profile point 3 at -grass_clearance = +0.08 over the unlifted edge; the lane edge at +0.10), not 15 cm. engine-july's prep holds the ground past the ROAD edge at the lane edge's height - 0.02 for 3 m (its contact band), so the 0.15 m strip lay in a 12-15 cm gutter with a wall of ground at its lip (0.1.5's gate OBJ at s 2,957 / 3,693: the strip -0.14 at +1.3 m, the ground -0.05..-0.13 at +1.4 and -0.02 at +1.8), and between the seam's points the ground climbed over the strip's lower half: the saw teeth on the fast curves' outsides. lm_intake._edge_fit_doc: ledger 0087 (Kevin 2026-11-07: "Milford should very smooth edges and they're ragged in places"): every built lane edge is the trace's width series (the ribbon is +-w/2 about the smoothed line), and the series is a 0.25 m-quantized NAIP-mask scan through a 21-station running median, a staircase. tools/edge_fit.py mode judge: per side, a robust local quadratic (+-15 m [invented]: at +-10 m the staircase still left 14 samples over 5 cm, at +-15 m none; a real width change here runs 20-50 m) through the trace's own samples, every 3-sigma candidate judged against the measured edge (source/edges/edge_evidence.json: NAIP 2022 + the 2017 lidar's intensity step): a 1-2 row spike the evidence does not support is cut, a sustained change stays; every verdict logged in data/edge_fit.json. The line is not moved
lm_intake._line_precomp_doc: ledger 0091, the Milford geometry audit's Gap 1 / Fix B (2026-11-18): the assembler's Gaussian (route.smooth_*) pulls the line inside every bend (sigma^2 / 2R) and sweeps the widths unchanged about it, so on the 27 % of the lap where both edge sensors agree the built centre sat 0.36 m (p50) / 1.01 m (p90) off the measured centre, the intake's own line 0.22 / 0.64 m. tools/lm_engine_intake.py, after the resample: x, z <- 2 P - S(P), S the route's own smooth, so the assembler builds ~P. Mac dry run (0091): 0.36 / 1.01 -> 0.24 / 0.68 m alone, lap 4,887 -> 4,898 m
lm_intake._edge_retrace_doc: 0.1.12, ledger 0087 Q1 (Kevin 2026-11-17: "Yes, widen Milford's front straight"): the front straight (s 4,530 -> 0 -> 150) re-traced to the measured pavement edge (tools/edge_retrace.py), never in, and never closer than 0.20 m [invented: the W-beam's face bulges 6.3 cm toward the road, and the assembler's own smoothing of the moved line shifts an edge up to ~9 cm (0.10 m left 1.2 cm on a proxy of 0.1.12 c2)] to G2's or G3's face; where G2 stands inside today's 16 m (s ~90-170, the 48 posts 0.1.11 left out on the lane) the lane stops at it so the rail stands whole. NAIP's edge, not the lidar's: along this light straight NAIP's points cluster within 0.1-0.2 m per 15 m and the image shows paving to them; the 2017 lidar's intensity step scatters 1-3 m and reads 0.8-2.5 m inside (both, row by row, in data/edge_retrace.json). A side that moves alone moves the line ((left - right) / 2); faded over 60 m [invented] at each end. LEDGER 0091 (2026-11-18), two records run in turn. (1) The front straight as above, two changes: shift_precomp (the line shift goes in as 2 D - S(D), so the assembler builds the shift measured, not its smoothed copy: with the line pre-compensated and sigma 7.5 m the uncompensated shift left G2's face 0.11 m off the lane edge, compensated 0.17 m, as 0.1.12's 0.167) and smooth_m / erode_m 12 / 12 [invented, the audit's Gap 7: the per-side edges smoothed more before the shift; Mac dry run: front-straight lateral jerk p95 at model speed 41.3 -> 36.5 m/s3 (no retrace at all: 34.3), the edge vs NAIP's points median 0.41 -> 0.48 m on the left; 8 / 10 keeps 0.40 at 49.6 m/s3, 12 / 15 gives 33.8 at 0.58]. (2) Mode agree over the eight stretches lm_intake.width_taper flared (stations on this line: where the source widths were widened, the audit's Gap 2 / Fix A: a one-sided gore or service-road mouth built two-sided, s 431-459, 1,228-1,237, 2,556-2,600, 2,638-2,675, 3,468-3,496, 3,909-3,919, 4,113-4,144, 4,224-4,249): each edge in OR out to the mean of NAIP and the lidar wherever their +-7.5 m medians agree within 0.6 m (edge_fit.AGREE_M, ledger 0087's rule), today's edge elsewhere; every rail of scenery.bespoke.rails listed for the clamp; the 60 m fade and 8 m smoothing as (1); erode_m 2.5 [invented, measured trade on the dry run: the far edge at s 435-455 / 2,545-2,560 ends +1.12 / +1.28 m out at 10 m, +0.76 / +0.80 at 5, +0.52 / +0.41 at 2.5, +0.45 / +0.20 at 0; agreed rows left > 0.25 m inside the sensors' reading 0 / 1 / 4 / 9 of ~450]; shift_precomp as (1)
lm_intake._measured_surface_doc: 0.1.12, fleet round 1 (Kevin 2026-11-13: "Milford still seems wavy as driven"): every line point's height and the bank from the G10's raw-lidar read of the lanes (board asset d74be8dc7f28b114c66f909ae18e2fcb; tools/measured_surface.py fit -> source/surface/road_surface.fit.json: a plane per 0.5 m station across -4.5..+4.5 m, low-passed flat above 30 m, cut below 15 m [invented: the lidar's 2-30 m content is its own ~1 cm noise], 60 / 30 m where the G10 flags noise_beats_signal). On 0.1.11 the lanes' 30-120 m waves were not the lidar's (2.5-4.6 cm RMS off at +-4.5 m), the bank's 30-300 m changes 0.5-1.1 % off, and two infield corners the lidar reads at 17-18 % (s 862-923, 991-1233) were built flat: the camber survey dropped every read over 12 %. deck_m 0.10 = build_loop_blend's ribbon lift (measured on 0.1.11: built centre - line Y, median 0.09999 m)
lm_intake._width_taper_doc: ledger 0078 round 5: the traced width jumps in one station at the gores (s 2,604: 12.2 -> 21.7 m); on the lidar bank drive_test's width-relative wheel paths re-seated across the slope there. Tapered at 0.1 m per m a side [invented: drive_test sets a wheel path from the width at the nearest line point (3 m), so a 0.3 m re-seat across a 10 % bank reads 3 cm in one 1 m sample: under the 3 % kink line]; widening only
lm_intake._width_smooth_doc: ledger 0091, the audit's Gap 3 / Fix C: the trace's width breathes at 20-80 m (98 / 212 mm RMS in the 20-40 / 40-80 m bands; High Plains' is a constant 12 m), both edges with it. A Gaussian of sigma 10 m [the audit's model, sim_widths.py: 20-40 m 98 -> 17 mm, 40-80 m 212 -> 131 mm on the whole lap] after edge_fit, before the retrace; the front straight's widen record keeps its own widths (its spans and taper, by its weight), the agree record re-traces its stretches over it. Mac dry run (0091, the whole config): 20-40 m 98 -> 46 mm, 40-80 m 212 -> 189 mm (the agree stretches' real narrowing is 40-80 m content), reversals 17.2 -> 14.3 / km
lm_intake._resample_doc: ledger 0078 round 5: rows every 1.5 m, not the trace's 3 m, so the s 990 corner's grade turns (R 15 m on -13.8 %) land half as hard on each row boundary; the line re-cut linearly, the smoothing doubled in points (the same in metres).
